property_summary: Rule: calling Put twice from the same EOA (non-reentrant) always leaves the contract callable again (locked_ reset) so two sequential Put calls succeed; the mutant that never resets locked_ causes the second Put call to revert/fail for some inputs (same caller), breaking this rule.

For any caller and any payable amount, after a successful Put(...) by that caller the contract remains callable again by the same caller (a second Put with the same caller and any payable amount must succeed); the mutant that never resets the reentrancy lock will make a subsequent Put call from the same caller fail for some inputs.

For any caller and any payable amount >= MinSum, a sequence of: (1) caller calls Put(amount) successfully, and then (2) the SAME caller calls Put(0) again succeeds (i.e., the contract remains callable after a Put) — the mutant that omits resetting the reentrancy lock causes the second Put to revert for some inputs (same caller and nonzero first call).

For any caller and any nonzero payable amount, after a successful Put(...) the contract remains callable again by that same caller so a subsequent Put(...) (even with zero value) succeeds; the mutant that never clears the reentrancy lock can leave the contract permanently non-callable for that caller, causing the second Put to fail for some inputs.

For any caller and any payable amount, a single successful Put(...) call must NOT permanently lock the contract: after a successful Put by an address, a subsequent Put from the same address must still be callable (i.e. not revert) — the mutant that omits resetting locked_ can permanently prevent further calls from that caller, causing the second Put to revert for some inputs.

After calling Put(_unlockTime) by any sender with any value, the stored unlockTime for that sender is always >= block.timestamp in the reference implementation; the mutant which sets acc.unlockTime to the lesser of _unlockTime and block.timestamp can store a value < block.timestamp and thus violates this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller and any Put(_unlockTime) call, the reference ensures Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime >= block.timestamp after Put returns; the mutant that stores the lesser of _unlockTime and block.timestamp can set unlockTime < block.timestamp for some _unlockTime, breaking this invariant.

After any successful Put called by an address with any value, the reference contract guarantees Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime >= block.timestamp, whereas the mutant that stores the lesser can produce Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any call to Put(_unlockTime) (with any msg.value), the reference contract ensures Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is never less than the _previous_ stored unlockTime (i.e., Put cannot decrease the caller's stored unlockTime), while the mutant that takes the lesser of _unlockTime and block.timestamp can decrease an existing unlockTime for some inputs and thus violates this monotonicity property.

For any caller and any call to Put(_unlockTime), the reference contract never decreases the caller's stored unlockTime (i.e., Acc[caller].unlockTime after Put is >= its value immediately before Put); the mutant that stores the lesser of _unlockTime and block.timestamp can decrease an existing unlockTime for some inputs, breaking this monotonicity.

For any caller and any positive msg.value, after calling Put(unlockTime) the caller's recorded Acc.balance increases by msg.value (so Acc[msg.sender].balance == previous_balance + msg.value); the mutant that omits updating acc.balance breaks this property for calls with msg.value>0.

For any caller and any msg.value, calling Put sets Acc[caller].balance to previous_balance + msg.value (the reference always records the deposited amount); the mutant that omits updating acc.balance violates this for some inputs with msg.value>0.

For any caller and any positive deposit amount, after calling Put the contract's public Acc mapping records that the caller's stored unlockTime is set to max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp) (this invariant depends only on the _unlockTime logic and not on whether balance is updated); the mutant that removed updating acc.balance still preserves unlockTime, so to catch the mutant we instead assert that when Put is called with msg.value > 0, the LogFile recorded a History entry reflecting the deposited value (the reference calls LogFile.AddMessage with msg.value while the mutant also does so — however this doesn't distinguish), therefore we instead choose a different universal property: calling Put with zero msg.value should not change the stored unlockTime or balance (i.e., a no-op when value==0) in the reference but the mutant also behaves same — to distinguish the mutant we use an adversarial caller that reverts when receiving ether and then call Put with a positive value through fallback; the reference still updates acc.balance because Put is executed, but the mutant fails to update balance — so the property: after invoking Put via fallback of a contract that forwards funds to C (i.e., C receives Ether through fallback which calls Put(0)), the recorded Acc balance for that caller equals the sent value (reference true for all inputs), which the mutant violates for some inputs.

For any caller and any positive ether amount sent in a direct payable Put call, the reference contract always increases Acc[caller].balance by the sent msg.value (balance_new == balance_old + msg.value); the mutant that omits updating acc.balance violates this for some inputs (msg.value>0).

For any caller and any nonzero msg.value, after calling Put(...) the contract's public Acc mapping records that Acc[caller].balance increased by exactly msg.value (i.e., new_balance == old_balance + msg.value); the mutant that removed the balance update breaks this rule for some inputs.
After a deposit by this test contract, a single Collect by the depositor cannot reduce the contract balance by more than the deposit amount (no reentrant extra drains).

property_summary: A direct call to Collect by this test account never reverts when the caller has sufficient on-contract balance and unlock time has passed (i.e., Collect should succeed if preconditions for withdrawal are met).
If the caller has at least MinSum deposited, requests to Collect an amount not exceeding their recorded balance after unlock time must not revert (no reentrant-induced revert for valid withdraws).

If this test contract has previously deposited at least MinSum and the target withdraw amount is <= that deposited balance and unlock time has passed, then a direct call to Collect must not revert (reverted == false).
If this test contract hasn't sent any prior funds to C, calling Collect must not revert (Collect should only be callable without revert by accounts that previously deposited and met conditions).

For any caller and amount, after a successful Collect(_) call the caller's recorded balance in C (Acc(caller).balance) is decreased by exactly the withdrawn amount; the mutant allowing reentrancy can violate this by reentering during Collect and causing the final recorded balance to be larger than expected.

After any successful Collect(amount) call by a holder, the holder's recorded Acc[holder].balance in the reference always decreases by exactly amount (i.e. final balance = initial balance - amount); the mutant removing the require allows reentrant Collect calls that can leave the recorded balance larger than expected for some inputs (attacker and amounts).

For any caller and withdraw amount where the caller previously deposited at least that amount and the unlock time has passed, a single call to Collect(amount) on the reference C never increases the contract's overall balance (address(c).balance) — the mutant that removes the nonReentrant require can reenter and cause more ETH to remain/return unexpectedly, producing a different final contract balance for some inputs.

For any depositor and withdraw amount, after a successful Collect(amount) call the caller's recorded Acc[caller].balance in the reference contract never increases compared to its value just before the call (i.e., final balance <= initial balance); removing the require enables reentrancy so for some attacker and amount the final recorded balance can be larger.

For every caller and withdraw amount where the caller previously deposited at least that amount and the unlock time has passed, a single call to Collect(amount) on the reference contract always leaves the caller's recorded Acc[caller].balance less than or equal to its value just before the call (it never increases); the mutant removing the nonReentrant_ require permits reentrant calls that can make Acc[caller].balance increase during Collect for some inputs/attacker.

For any caller and any amount that meets the preconditions (balance >= MinSum, balance >= amount, and now > unlockTime), after Collect(amount) completes the caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance in the correct contract equals its prior balance minus amount; the mutant that decrements balance before the external call can be observed to leave Acc[msg.sender].balance inconsistent when the external transfer to the caller fails (or reverts) — i.e., the invariant that balance is only reduced when the Ether was successfully sent is violated by the mutant.

Invariant: Collect only reduces Acc[msg.sender].balance when the external payout succeeds; the mutant that decrements balance before performing the external call can leave Acc[msg.sender].balance reduced even when the external transfer fails, violating this rule.

For any caller and amount, Collect only decrements the caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance when the external transfer of Ether to msg.sender actually succeeds; the mutant that updates state before the external call can decrement the balance even when the external transfer fails (e.g., because the callee reverts), breaking this rule.

Collect only reduces Acc[msg.sender].balance when the external transfer to msg.sender succeeds; the mutant that decrements acc.balance before the external call can leave Acc[msg.sender].balance reduced even if the external transfer reverts.
